config.title: Form Library from Scratch

intro.title: Form Library from Scratch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form library from scratch in Angular to understand how form controls and validation work under the hood. You'll learn the core concept of reactive programming by creating a FormControl class that manages state and updates. The main technologies involved are TypeScript for type safety and Angular's dependency injection and change detection. You'll implement basic features like setting values, tracking validity, and handling user input changes. By the end, you'll have a foundational custom form control that you can extend with more advanced features.
intro.usecase: Building custom form libraries is essential for enterprise applications where standard form solutions don't meet complex validation, accessibility, or design system requirements. Developers implement these patterns in customer relationship management (CRM) systems, financial dashboards, and healthcare portals that need consistent form behavior across hundreds of input fields. For example, a banking application's loan approval form requires custom validation logic, real-time field dependencies, and specialized error messaging that off-the-shelf libraries can't provide. Creating your own form library gives teams complete control over form state management, validation rules, and integration with backend APIs while maintaining consistent user experience across the entire application.

objectives: Construct a custom form control component with validation logic
Implement reactive form binding between template inputs and component state
Configure form validation rules and error message display
Initialize and manage form state using Angular's lifecycle hooks
Integrate form submission handling with data processing
Manipulate form values and validation status programmatically
Render dynamic form structures based on configuration data

steps.title: Import Component, FormsModule, and ReactiveFormsModule from Angular
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core', and FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule from '@angular/forms'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in these Angular modules. They are needed for creating components and handling forms.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component from '@angular/core', and FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule from '@angular/forms'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular modules are imported, setting up the foundation for the form library.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core', and FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule are imported from '@angular/forms'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but make sure to import all three: Component, FormsModule, and ReactiveFormsModule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import Component from '@angular/core', and FormsModule and ReactiveFormsModule from '@angular/forms'.

steps.title: Create the main FormLibraryComponent class
steps.instruction: Create a FormLibraryComponent class with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define the component. Set the selector and template properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class is defined with the @Component decorator, a selector, and an empty template.
successCriteria: FormLibraryComponent class is created with @Component decorator, selector, and empty template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the @Component decorator with selector and template properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you're using @Component with selector and template.

steps.title: Initialize FormGroup for user registration
steps.instruction: In the FormLibraryComponent class, declare a form property of type FormGroup and initialize it with a new FormGroup containing empty controls for 'name' and 'email'.
steps.hint: You'll need to import FormGroup from '@angular/forms' and create a new FormGroup instance in the component's constructor or ngOnInit.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a form property properly typed as FormGroup and initialized with controls for name and email.
successCriteria: FormGroup is imported, a form property of type FormGroup is declared, and it's initialized with a FormGroup containing 'name' and 'email' controls.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported FormGroup, declared the property with the correct type, and initialized it with controls for both 'name' and 'email'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form property isn't properly set up. Remember to import FormGroup, declare the property with type FormGroup, and initialize it with controls for name and email fields.

steps.title: Define form controls with validation rules
steps.instruction: Inside the FormLibraryComponent class, add three FormControl instances for 'name', 'email', and 'password' fields, each with the required validator.
steps.hint: Use the FormControl constructor with an initial empty string and the Validators.required validator. Remember to import Validators from '@angular/forms' if needed.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form group will have three controls with validation rules, ready for user input.
successCriteria: The form group contains FormControl instances for name, email, and password, each with Validators.required applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some controls, but make sure all three fields (name, email, password) have FormControl instances with Validators.required.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form controls are not properly defined. Ensure you create FormControl instances for name, email, and password with the required validator inside the form group.

steps.title: Create the onSubmit handler method
steps.instruction: Inside the FormLibraryComponent class, define a method named onSubmit that logs the form's current values to the console when called.
steps.hint: Add a method to the class that uses console.log to output this.form.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an onSubmit method that logs form values when invoked.
successCriteria: The FormLibraryComponent class contains an onSubmit method that logs this.form.value to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it's named 'onSubmit' and logs the form values using console.log(this.form.value).
steps.feedbackWrong: The onSubmit method is not correctly defined. Check that it's inside the class and properly logs the form values.

steps.title: Add the form container with formGroup binding
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a <form> element with [formGroup] binding to the 'form' property and (ngSubmit) event binding to the 'onSubmit' method.
steps.hint: Use the [formGroup] directive to bind the form element to your FormGroup instance, and (ngSubmit) to handle form submission.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a <form> element with proper bindings to the FormGroup and submission handler.
successCriteria: The template includes a <form> element with [formGroup]="form" and (ngSubmit)="onSubmit()".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your <form> element has both [formGroup] and (ngSubmit) bindings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form element is missing or doesn't have the correct bindings. Check the syntax for [formGroup] and (ngSubmit).

steps.title: Add name input field with formControlName
steps.instruction: Inside the component's template, add an <input> element for the name field with formControlName='name' and a placeholder attribute.
steps.hint: Use the formControlName directive to bind the input to the 'name' control defined in your FormGroup.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: input binding in Angular -->
<input type="text" formControlName="username" placeholder="Enter username">
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain an input field for the name control, connected via formControlName.
successCriteria: An <input> element with formControlName='name' and a placeholder attribute is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input, but make sure it has formControlName='name' and a placeholder.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input for the name field is missing or incorrectly configured. Check the formControlName binding.

steps.title: Add email input field with formControlName
steps.instruction: In the template, add an email input field with formControlName='email' and type='email'.
steps.hint: Add the input element inside the form container, similar to the name field but with email-specific attributes.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: email input with form binding -->
<input type="email" formControlName="email" placeholder="Enter your email">
steps.expectedOutcome: The email input field is added to the form with proper binding to the 'email' FormControl.
successCriteria: The template contains an <input> element with formControlName='email' and type='email'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input, but check that it has both formControlName='email' and type='email'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The email input is missing or incorrectly configured. Ensure it uses formControlName='email' and type='email'.

steps.title: Add password input field with formControlName
steps.instruction: Add an <input> element for the password field inside the form, below the email input. Set its type to 'password', add the formControlName attribute with value 'password', and include a placeholder text.
steps.hint: The password input should be similar to the name and email inputs you already added, but with type='password' and formControlName='password'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a password input with formControlName
<input type="password" formControlName="password" placeholder="Enter your password">
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a password input field that is connected to the 'password' FormControl, with validation for required and minimum length.
successCriteria: An <input> element with type='password', formControlName='password', and a placeholder attribute is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input, but check that it has type='password', formControlName='password', and a placeholder.
steps.feedbackWrong: The password input is missing or incorrect. Ensure you add an <input> with type='password' and formControlName='password' inside the form.

steps.title: Add submit button wired to onSubmit
steps.instruction: Inside the form element, add a submit button with the text 'Submit' that will trigger the form submission.
steps.hint: Use a button element with type='submit' inside the form. The form's ngSubmit event is already bound to onSubmit().
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: submit button in a form -->
<button type="submit">Submit Form</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A submit button appears in the form that, when clicked, triggers the onSubmit() method and logs the form data if valid.
successCriteria: The form contains a button element with type='submit' and appropriate text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check if it has type='submit' and is inside the form element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The submit button is missing or incorrectly placed. Add a button with type='submit' inside the form.

steps.title: Add reset button wired to onReset
steps.instruction: Add a reset button inside the form, after the submit button, with a (click) event binding that calls the onReset() method.
steps.hint: Place the button element inside the form tags, after the existing submit button. Use the (click) event binding to trigger the onReset method.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: button with click handler -->
<button type="button" (click)="handleReset()">Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a reset button that clears all input fields when clicked.
successCriteria: A reset button with (click)="onReset()" is added inside the form after the submit button.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has (click)="onReset()" and is placed inside the form.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset button is missing or not correctly wired. Add a button with (click)="onReset()" inside the form.
